name: United Kingdom
summary_text: The United Kingdom has a documented, in-force rollback concentrated on facilities and detention that directly affects trans visitors. Bathroom and changing-room use is now directed by biological sex under the Equality watchdog's statutory code — a daily, nationwide civil restriction (the UK is the only country above 0.55 in this dataset with a nationally-legislated bathroom restriction). Since the April 2025 Supreme Court ruling, two severe-when-triggered risks apply if arrested: police forces strip-search trans women according to biological sex (with male officers), and trans women are placed in men's prisons — with documented suicide-risk litigation. Documented trans killings have occurred (Brianna Ghey, 2023, and others). The climate is actively deteriorating via courts/EHRC-led rollback (not executive demonization — a contrast with the United States). The UK's traveler-relevant positives are limited: no trans-specific border friction (foreign passports with X or amended markers are accepted), hate-crime law covering gender identity (theoretical recourse), no criminalisation, and functional institutions. The Gender Recognition Certificate and marriage equality — previously cited as positives — are resident-facing and do not apply to visitors.

sources.title: Judge rules Scottish guidance for housing trans prisoners is unlawful - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: BBC (June 2026): a Scottish judge ruled the Scottish Prison Service guidance allowing some trans prisoners to be housed in jails matching their gender identity unlawful - sex segregation in prisons must be based on biological sex, following the UK Supreme Court's April 2025 'definition of a woman' ruling.

sources.title: Suicide risk if trans prisoners are put in jails based on sex at birth, court told - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: BBC (Feb 2026): in the same litigation, government lawyers argued that requiring trans prisoners to be held according to sex at birth would breach human rights and create an unacceptable suicide risk; the Supreme Court ruling loomed over the case.

sources.title: British Transport Police amends strip-searching policy after supreme court gender ruling | Rail transport | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (April 2025): British Transport Police amended its strip-searching policy after the Supreme Court gender ruling - trans women would be strip-searched by male officers as an 'interim position', directly affecting trans travellers on UK railways.

sources.title: Police Scotland publishes interim transgender search guidance - Police Scotland
sources.claim_summary: Police Scotland (June 2025): interim guidance on searching transgender persons and by transgender officers - searches involving removal of more than a jacket, gloves, headgear or footwear will be conducted on the basis of biological sex, following the UK Supreme Court judgment on the Equality Act.

sources.title: Crash Krylova: Trans People in Prison: For Women Scotland v Scottish Ministers [2026] CSOH 59 – UK Constitutional Law Association
sources.claim_summary: UK Constitutional Law Association analysis (July 2026) of For Women Scotland v Scottish Ministers [2026] CSOH 59: critique of the judgment striking down the Scottish Prison Service's trans-custody policy, covering the Equality Act, Prison Rules, the Gender Recognition Act 2004 and Article 8.

sources.title: New guidance on single-sex spaces comes into force
sources.claim_summary: BBC (Aug 2026): the EHRC's updated code of practice on single-sex spaces came into force in England, Wales and Scotland - single-sex facilities such as toilets and changing rooms should be organised based on biological sex; trans people should use gender-neutral facilities or those matching their biological sex. Applies to cafes, leisure centres, public toilets, shelters and more.

TransActual UK 'Gendered Spaces Report 2025': documents trans people's experiences of accessing gendered spaces in the UK amid the hostile post-Supreme-Court environment, alongside related research (Trans Lives 2025, healthcare reports).

sources.title: UN experts warn revised UK Equality Act puts transgender people at risk - JURIST - News
sources.claim_summary: JURIST (Aug 2026): UN human rights experts warned that the UK's revised Equality Act Code of Practice (statutory from 5 August 2026) risks institutionalised discrimination - it advises that single-sex services must either exclude trans women or admit men, 'effectively presenting exclusion as a means of' legal compliance.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying document is Surrey Police's searching/biological-sex policy (FOI release).

sources.title: Criminal Justice Act 2003
sources.claim_summary: legislation.gov.uk: the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (as hosted on the old OPSI site) - primary UK legislation; Part 12 includes provisions relevant to sexual-offence sentencing reform following the 2003 overhaul that replaced older laws applied disproportionately to gay men.
